Base directory for this skill: /Users/bgauduch/Obsidian Vault/.claude/skills/add-editorial-visual

# Add Editorial Visual

Generate a branded editorial visual (HTML->PNG) for a piece. Format dispatch (`square` / `event-banner`) per design-system §5.0 registry. Content FR.

The HTML skeleton fixes the frame + CSS components; the layout engine (flex/grid) handles geometry. Claude assembles **semantic blocks**, never absolute coordinates. A **legibility gate by visual inspection** + brand-review lock the result.

## SSoT - read at runtime, never restate

| Concern | Source |
|---|---|
| Visual-format registry (format → dims, ratio, spec §, skeleton, naming, home) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/03-Design-system.md` §5.0 |
| Per-format design spec (square zones/recipes §5.4, event-banner §5.6) | `03-Design-system.md` §5.4 / §5.6 |
| Color tokens + WCAG ratios | `03-Design-system.md` §1.1 / §1.2 |
| Executable skeleton (frame + classes + slots), per format | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/skeletons/<format>.html` |
| HTML->PNG renderer | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/CLAUDE.md` Asset pipelines (`render-html.mjs`) |
| Asset naming, piece link | `02-Areas/Éditorial/CLAUDE.md` |

Reverse-engineering from an existing asset is forbidden (BGA CLAUDE.md Asset production contract). The skeleton is the only structural base.

## Input

`--piece <path>` (required). Visual SSoT input = the piece's `## Visuels` section.
`--format <visual-format>` (optional): overrides the brief's `format` (enum `visual-format`, `02-Areas/Éditorial/enums.yml`; specs §5.0). Default `square` if absent from brief.
`--kind <disposition>` (optional, square only): shortcut overriding the brief's disposition. Disposition enum (recipes -> design-system §5.4).

## Workflow

### 1. Read the piece + visual brief
- Read the piece. Extract the `## Visuels` section: per visual `nature`, `format`, `disposition` (square only), `intention`, `point de départ (setup/Why)`, `contenu (How)`, `synthèse (solution/What)`, `bonus`, `asset cible`.
- `nature: capture` → out of scope (capture supplied by the user); only handle `nature: schéma`.
- Brief absent or empty → ask the user for **format + intention + contenu** (and disposition/setup/synthèse/bonus if relevant), then **write them back into the piece's `## Visuels`** (durable capture, idempotent re-run) before continuing.
- `--format` overrides the brief's `format` (default `square`); `--kind` overrides the disposition (square only).

### 2. Derive text zones (deterministic)
- **Kicker**: breadcrumb `<DOMAIN> · <SUBDOMAIN> · <SUBJECT>` derived from the piece's `tags` / `pillar`, uppercase (§5.4).
- **H1**: short visual title (from `intention` or the piece H1). `accent-soft` emphasis (`<span class="hl">`) on the key fragment: **mandatory**.
- **Lead**: framing sentence (1 line).
- **Footer suffix**: `· <SPE1> · <SPE2>`, same domain as the kicker (top/bottom consistency §5.4).

### 3. Clone the skeleton (per format)
- Resolve skeleton by format: `Brand/skeletons/<format>.html` (§5.0). Copy → `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/<format>-<subject>.html` (`<subject>` kebab-case, naming §5.0).
- Collision → suffix `-2` and warn.

### 4. Fill the slots (semantic HTML, never coordinates)
Replace the content between markers `<!-- slot:<zone>:start -->` / `<!-- slot:<zone>:end -->` (never by line number). Missing/orphan marker → explicit abort, no fallback. **Slots are format-specific** (use the skeleton's own markers): `event-banner` → `kicker` (`LIVE TECH · <date>`), `title` (with `<span class="hl">`), `subtitle` (framing line) - §5.6, then skip to step 5. `square` → the zones below (§5.4).
- `slot:kicker`, `slot:h1` (with `<span class="hl">`), `slot:lead`, `slot:footer-suffix`: text from step 2.
- `slot:content`: assemble with the skeleton's **component classes**, following the **Why → How → What arc**:
	- `.setup` (Why) if the brief provides a starting point;
	- body (How) per the **disposition** (`comparaison` → `.cols` with two `.wf`; `verticale`/`cycle-de-vie` → sequence of `.step` + `.arrow`; cf recipes §5.4);
	- `.synth` (What) if the brief provides a synthesis; `.bonus` (labelled inset on cream) if the brief calls for it. Synthesis and bonus = **distinct** zones: merge one into the other only on explicit brief instruction.
	- **Brief fidelity**: render **one `.step` per enumerated step** in the `contenu (How)`; never merge or cap the number of steps. The skeleton's reference markup (2 steps) is illustrative, not a limit.
	- Terminal state cards `.result.is-danger|.is-success` with `.rhead` (Lucide icon + title) and `.pill` (≥14px bold). Technical values (ARN, RoleId, keys) in `.mono`.
- Compose HTML that lays itself out: no fixed heights/positions, text must be able to wrap. Keep content concise to fit the frame (the engine does not shrink the font).

### 5. Render PNG
`node "02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/_pipeline/render-html.mjs" <html> <png-same-base> <W> <H>` where `<W> <H>` = the format's dimensions (§5.0 registry). Output `<format>-<subject>.png` (@2x).

### 6. Legibility gate (visual inspection) — blocking
**Read the rendered PNG** (Read tool on the .png) and check visually:
- no overlap, no text outside its frame or truncated, no stacked elements;
- legible hierarchy (kicker < h1, distinct zones);
- structure matches the brief (setup/workflows/synthesis present if requested), Why→How→What arc legible.
Any anomaly → fix the HTML (concision, structure), re-render. The PNG is authoritative, not the HTML.

### 7. Brand-review gate
Run the `brand-review` skill: `--visual <html> --visual-png <png> --text <piece>`.
- Pre-check (blocking, ADR-001 - the procedure lives in `check-colors.mjs`, never restated here): `node "02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/_pipeline/check-colors.mjs" <html>`.
- Verdict ≠ PRÊT (incl. V9 legibility) → fix, re-render, re-review. Steps 6+7: max 3 loops, then surface the residual.

### 8. Wire the piece (idempotent)
In `## Visuels`, add the rendered link `[[<format>-<subject>.png]]` to the relevant visual (under its brief). Re-run with the same asset = no-op.
The `assets[]` frontmatter field stays out of scope (data governance task #4): body link only.

- html + png paths.
- Format + disposition (square) chosen + slots filled + arc zones used (setup/synthesis/bonus).
- Legibility gate: OK | fixed (n loops).
- Brand-review verdict (+ manual residuals).
- `## Visuels` wiring: applied | already present. Brief rewritten: yes/no.

## Rules
- Skeleton = structural SSoT. No reverse-engineering of existing assets; changing the frame = amend §5.0/§5.4/§5.6 + the skeleton first.
- **Layout delegated to CSS**: never absolute positioning, never hand-computed coordinates. Compose semantic blocks with the skeleton classes.
- Colors = closed whitelists: hex §1.1, translucent derivatives §1.1bis. Missing value → STOP, amend the design-system. Alpha never on ink.
- Text on light background respects WCAG §1.2. The amber accent token is decorative only (rules, bars, arrows), never text (§7).
- The rendered PNG is authoritative: an illegible visual is never delivered, even if tokens/WCAG pass.
- One visual = one asset `<format>-<subject>.{html,png}` (§5.0). Capture = `capture-<subject>.png`, supplied outside the skill.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/bgauduch/Obsidian Vault/.claude/skills/brand-review

# brand-review

Validate a BGA editorial artifact (LinkedIn post, blog draft, visual asset) against brand SSoT before publication.

## SSoT - read, never restate

| Concern | Doc |
|---|---|
| Voice, lexicon, principles 2.1-2.10, format §4.1, check-list §7 | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md` |
| Color tokens §1.1, translucent derivatives §1.1bis, WCAG ratios §1.2, typo §2, components §6 | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/03-Design-system.md` |
| V3 + V4 procedure (executable, reads the three sections at runtime) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/_pipeline/check-colors.mjs` |
| Per-support specs (cadence, hook, hashtags, CTA, format) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/06-Roadmap-declinaisons.md` |
| Positioning, anti-positions, brand adjectives | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/01-Brief.md` |

Inheritance: editorial CLAUDE.md (`02-Areas/Éditorial/CLAUDE.md`), incl. its per-channel publication tactics.

## Inputs

- `--visual "02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/event-banner-terraform-refactoring.html" --visual-png "02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/event-banner-terraform-refactoring.png" --text "02-Areas/Éditorial/Pieces/2026-08-25 Live - Refactoring avec Terraform.md"` = one or two paths. Detect type by extension:
  - `.md` → text artifact
  - `.svg` / `.html` / `.png` → visual artifact
- If only one path: audit that dimension only.
- If both: also check text/visual coherence (same kicker, same key terms, no contradiction).
- If none: ask user for path(s).

## Workflow

1. Read inputs + the four SSoT docs above (relevant sections only).
2. Run text audit (if applicable).
3. Run visual audit (if applicable).
4. Run coherence check (if both).
5. Output status table + single prioritized recommendation.

## Text audit criteria

| # | Check | Pass condition |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | Principle 2.7 - tournure positive | Affirmative dominant; negative only for Do/Don't, anti-positions, blocking rules, idioms, external quotes |
| T2 | No em-dash | Zero `—` characters |
| T3 | Hook §4.1 | First 1-2 lines: chiffré or scénario concret, no buzzword opener |
| T4 | Structure §4.1 | Hook / Contexte / Insight / CTA discret ordering |
| T5 | CTA §4.1 | Discret ("je veux bien en discuter", "curieux de vos cas"), pas "DM-moi" |
| T6 | Lexicon §3.2 | Brand adjectives respected, anti-positions absent (hype, dark-tech-bro, corporate-consulting, jargon non explicité) |
| T7 | Hashtags | 3-5 max, on-topic |
| T8 | Anglais tech §3.3 | Identifiants réels (`AttachPolicy`, `SCP`, EventBridge) OK ; concept forgé → terme FR (gel sélectif, pas *blast hybride*) ; pas de franglais gratuit |
| T9 | Dates | Format `YYYY-MM-DD` partout |
| T10 | Check-list §7 | Tous les items applicables cochés |
| T11 | Arc narratif §2.9 | Golden Circle Why->How->What, ouverture sur tension/*pourquoi* ; pas d'outside-in (ouverture sur le *quoi*) ni liste sans fil |
| T12 | Calques + auto-qualification | Zéro idiome EN traduit littéralement, métaphore ancrée à son objet (§3.3 calque interdit) ; zéro auto-qualificatif (§2.11) ; vouvoiement par défaut, header de série sur post de live (§4.1) |
| T13 | Registre participatif §2.10 | Action partagée (live, démo, atelier, pas-à-pas) au "on" inclusif ; "je" réservé aux 3 cas légitimes de §2.10 (aside d'auteur, décision assumée, aveu), jamais l'action clavier. Signal d'échec : "je" majoritaire sur les actions partagées |
| T14 | Forme §4.1 | Une idée par bloc ou par ligne ; gestes, démos et étapes en liste. Signaux d'échec : un bloc portant plusieurs idées, une énumération de gestes courant inline dans une phrase |

## Visual audit criteria

| # | Check | Pass condition |
|---|---|---|
| V1 | Format §6 LinkedIn | 1200x1200 (carré) ou ratio support attendu |
| V2 | Background | Token de fond ou de surface de §1.1 (lue au runtime), jamais une valeur choisie hors table |
| V3 | Tokens couleur §1.1 + §1.1bis | **Exécuté**, jamais jugé à l'œil : `node "02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/_pipeline/check-colors.mjs" <html[?query]> [--pdf]`. Hex ∈ §1.1, `rgba()` ∈ §1.1bis, alpha jamais sur l'encre, aucun alpha sur un chemin de livraison PDF. Exit 1 = échec. Une exemption se déclare sur la ligne (`brand-exempt: <raison>`), jamais en silence |
| V4 | WCAG §1.2 sur composite | Même commande, seconde passe : le fond de chaque texte est **mesuré au rendu** (pire pixel sous la boîte), pas déduit du token de fond nominal. Un dérivé §1.1bis « porteur » change le ratio réel. Un texte décoratif doit porter `data-decor` pour être exempté. L'ambre accent est décoratif, jamais en texte (§7) |
| V5 | Typo §2 | Manrope pour titres/body, JetBrains Mono pour code/identifiants techniques |
| V6 | Hiérarchie | Kicker → H1 → H2 → body, weights conformes (kicker 600, h1 800, h2 700, body 400) |
| V7 | Logo / signature | Footer présent si support le requiert (`06-Roadmap-declinaisons.md`) |
| V8 | Accent bar | Top-left amber bar 80x4 (signature visuelle BGA) |
| V9 | Lisibilité / layout | **Inspection du PNG rendu** (Read sur le .png) : aucun chevauchement, aucun texte hors cadre ni tronqué, aucun élément superposé, hiérarchie lisible. Conformité tokens/WCAG ne vaut PAS validation visuelle. **Bloquant** : un visuel illisible n'est jamais PRÊT |
| V10 | Arc narratif (si setup) | Quand le brief prévoit un point de départ : ancrage *Why* (setup) + synthèse *What* présents, arc Why->How->What lisible (principe 2.9, §5.4) |

Tokens, dérivés et ratios = SSoT `03-Design-system.md` §1.1 / §1.1bis / §1.2, lues au runtime **par le checker**. Aucune valeur recopiée ici, et aucune énumération refaite à la main : V3 et V4 se lisent dans la sortie de `check-colors.mjs`.

Points de vigilance (appliquer §1.2, ne pas deviner) :
- Texte d'état sur fond soft (success/warning/danger sur leur soft) : vérifier le seuil large/bold de §1.2 ; les petits labels/pills doivent atteindre la taille/graisse requise, sinon échec.
- **Ambre-sur-ambre** (warning/accent sur `accent-soft`/soft) = zone molle : contrôler le ratio §1.2 ou déplacer le complément sur fond crème (cf §5.4 bonus). Ne jamais présumer que ça passe.

## Coherence check (when both provided)

- Kicker visual == thèmes du texte
- H1/H2 visual reprend une phrase-clé du texte
- Étapes/garde-fous visuels alignés avec les bullets du texte
- Aucun terme dans le visuel qui n'apparaît pas dans le texte (et vice-versa pour les key terms)

## Output format

```
# Brand review - <artifact name(s)> - YYYY-MM-DD

## Texte
| # | Critère | Statut | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Tournure positive | ✅/⚠️/❌ | <one-liner si non ✅> |
...

## Visuel
| # | Critère | Statut | Note |
...

## Cohérence texte/visuel (si applicable)
- ...

## Recommandation prioritaire
<une seule action, la plus impactante>

## Verdict
PRÊT / À RETOUCHER / À RETRAVAILLER
```

## Rules

- Read SSoT before judging; never invent specs.
- Cite section number (e.g., "§4.1", "principe 2.7") in notes.
- One recommendation max - the user picks one fix per round, not a backlog.
- French output (artifact language); English only inside this SKILL.md.
- V3/V4 are the checker's output, never a hand-rolled grep: a hex grep is blind to `rgba()`, which is exactly the gap `check-colors.mjs` was built to close. Standalone SVG (no HTML wrapper) has no rendered pass; enumerate its `fill`/`stroke` against §1.1 and §1.1bis and say so in the note.
- This skill is the single home of the check procedure (ADR-001). The create skills call the checker, they never restate it.

1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	Guidance for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, Aider, etc.) working in this repository. A `CLAUDE.md` symlink points here so Claude Code picks it up automatically. Each example also has its own nested `AGENTS.md` with example-specific guidance - read it before editing inside an example.
4	
5	## What this repo is
6	
7	A **library of self-contained Terraform examples**. Each lives under `examples/<name>/` and is independent: its own `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, tooling (`mise.toml`, `.tflint.hcl`) and Terraform root module(s). Examples are **not** factored into shared code - isolation is intentional so each can be read, run, and live-demoed on its own.
8	
9	Use cases served: reusable patterns, illustrations for blog/LinkedIn posts, and starting points / labs for live tech sessions.
10	
11	## Taxonomy
12	
13	Every example declares a primary `type` plus free-form tags. Source of truth is the catalogue table in the root `README.md`; each example's `README.md`/`AGENTS.md` restates its type.
14	
15	- `pattern` - reusable, production-leaning reference.
16	- `lab` - starting point / TP with progressive steps for a live session.
17	- `experiment` - preview/RC features, may be intentionally unstable.
18	
19	Do **not** create top-level category directories (`patterns/`, `experiments/`...). Keep `examples/` flat and classify via `type` + tags. This avoids lifecycle churn when an example changes category.
20	
21	## How to add an example (golden path)
22	
23	1. `mkdir examples/<name>/` - kebab-case, scope-first (`aws-multi-env`, `terraform-rc-variables`).
24	2. Add `README.md` (state its `type` + tags, objective, run steps, and a closing `## References`
25	   section) and `AGENTS.md` (example-specific guidance).
26	   - `## References` is **mandatory**: link the authoritative docs for every mechanism the example
27	     demonstrates - HashiCorp for language/CLI features, the provider registry for data sources and
28	     resources, AWS docs for the service behaviour a reader will hit. One line each, saying what
29	     the link answers rather than repeating its title. Verify each URL resolves before committing:
30	     these READMEs are read on screen and a 404 is noticed.
31	   - Keep it distinct from `## Going further`, which cross-references sibling examples and adjacent
32	     approaches rather than documentation.
33	   - `## Troubleshooting` is optional in general, and **mandatory for any example creating an
34	     `aws_cloudwatch_log_group`**: a resolver that blackholes `logs.*` stops the apply halfway with
35	     a misleading network error. See `tasks/lessons.md` (Local environment) for the bullet to carry.
36	3. Add per-example tooling: `mise.toml` (pins `terraform`, may be an RC/prerelease for `experiment` types; inherits `tflint`/`trivy` from the repo-root `mise.toml`) and `.tflint.hcl`.
37	4. Add the Terraform root module(s). Any directory containing a `providers.tf` is auto-discovered by CI - no CI edit needed to validate it.
38	5. Register a row in the root `README.md` catalogue table.
39	
40	## CI
41	
42	`.github/workflows/terraform.yml` auto-discovers Terraform root modules (directories containing `providers.tf`) under `examples/` and runs `validate` + `tflint` + `trivy` per module in a matrix. `terraform fmt -check -recursive` runs once at the root. The `tf-setup` composite action installs the toolchain via `jdx/mise-action` from the target module's merged `mise.toml` (terraform, tflint, trivy). Adding an example requires no CI change.
43	
44	## Toolchain (mise)
45	
46	[mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) is the **single source of truth (SSOT)** for every CLI tool, locally and in CI - there is no separate version file or per-tool CI setup step.
47	
48	- **Root `mise.toml`** pins repo-wide tools (`tflint`, `trivy`) plus a default `terraform`. **Per-example `mise.toml`** overrides only `terraform` (versions legitimately differ per example) and inherits the rest, since mise merges every `mise.toml` from the cwd up to the repo root.
49	- **Add a new tool once, in `mise.toml`** (root if repo-wide, example if local). Never re-pin a tool as a CI input - CI installs whatever `mise.toml` declares.
50	- **Renovate** bumps these via its native `mise` manager; alpha/beta/rc pins (e.g. `experiment` examples) are frozen by a `packageRule` matching `currentValue`.
51	- **Tasks replace Makefiles**: run with `mise run <task>`, list with `mise tasks`. Each task runs in a subshell, so a task's `cd` (or `dir`) never leaks into your interactive shell.
52	- **Locally**: `mise install` once, then tools resolve automatically per directory (use `mise exec -- <cmd>`, or activate mise in your shell).
53	
54	## Repository standards
55	
56	- **Language**: English everywhere in committed content - code, comments, identifiers, docs, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, script output strings. No other language, including inside an example. (This repo is read on screen and public; mixed languages stand out.)
57	- **Git flow**: GitHub flow (short-lived feature branches off `main`, PR review, squash-merge). Name branches `<type>/<kebab-summary>` where `<type>` is a Conventional Commit type (`feat`, `fix`, `build`, `ci`, `docs`, `chore`, `refactor`, `test`) - e.g. `build/mise-toolchain-ssot` - so branch names stay consistent with commit messages and PR titles.
58	- **Work tracking**: durable backlog = GitHub Issues + Milestone (a goal + its acceptance criteria); each PR references its issue (`Closes #N`). `main` carries no task file - session plans stay local/ephemeral. `tasks/lessons.md` holds durable repo lessons.
59	- **Commit messages**: [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) - `<type>(<scope>): <subject>`. Use the example name as scope when relevant (e.g. `feat(aws-multi-env): ...`).
60	  - Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `chore`, `refactor`, `test`, `ci`, `build`.
61	  - Breaking changes: append `!` after type/scope or add a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
62	  - Keep subject imperative, lowercase, no trailing period, ~72 chars max.
63	  - Enforced in CI: `commitlint.yml` (commit messages, config-conventional) and `pr-title.yml` (semantic PR title, since squash-merge uses the PR title).
64	- **Versioning**: [SemVer](https://semver.org/), repo-level single release line via release-please.
65	- **Validation before commit**: `terraform fmt -recursive` (root) and `terraform validate` inside each touched root module. Optional local mirror of the CI gates lives in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (fmt/validate/tflint + conventional commit-msg); enable with `pre-commit install --install-hooks && pre-commit install --hook-type commit-msg`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Overlay a step snapshot into live/ - the state stays put, only the .tf files
# change. This replaces live commenting/uncommenting during a demo.
set -euo pipefail

step="${1:?usage: switch.sh <step-1|step-2|step-3|step-4|step-5|step-5b|step-6>}"
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
src="$root/$step"

[ -d "$src" ] || { echo "unknown step: $step" >&2; exit 1; }

rm -f "$root"/live/*.tf
cp "$src"/*.tf "$root/live/"

echo "live/ is now at $step (state untouched)."
echo "next: cd live && terraform init && terraform plan"

# AGENTS.md - terraform-state-refactoring

Example-specific guidance. Read the repo-root `AGENTS.md` first.

## What this example is

`lab` - progressive steps demonstrating declarative state refactoring: `moved`
blocks (rename, split to a module, for_each set, versioned module migrations,
chained moves), then the cross-state handover (`removed` + `import`).

## Layout contract

- `live/` is the **only** root that ever holds a real state. It starts as a copy
  of `step-1` and mutates during a session via `scripts/switch.sh <step>`.
- `step-1` .. `step-6` (+ `step-5b`) are **complete snapshots**, one per gesture.
  All are CI-validated. A step change means updating BOTH the snapshot and, if
  it is the starting point, `live/`.
- Step dirs sit at the same depth as `live/` on purpose: module sources
  (`../modules/app-config/vN`) resolve identically before and after a switch.
  Do not nest them under a `steps/` folder.
- `modules/app-config/{v1,v2,v3}` simulate published module versions. v2 and v3
  ship `moved.tf` + `MIGRATION.md`: that pairing IS the lesson - never strip a
  `moved` block from a version, the chain is the upgrade path.
- `adjacent/` is a second, independent state (the billing team's root) used by
  the step-6 handover.

## Rules

- Parameter names and values must stay identical across steps: every step's
  target is a plan with **zero resource changes** (moves/forgets only). A diff
  that touches infrastructure is a bug in the step.
- Keep resources to SSM parameters: fast, near-free, no teardown traps.
- The repo never references the live sessions that use it (decoupling rule).

# Terraform state refactoring - `moved`, `removed`, `import`

`lab` · tags: `terraform` `state` `moved` `removed` `import` `refactoring` `modules` `v1.7`

Refactor a live root module **without destroying anything**: rename a resource,
split the root into a platform-team module, absorb a `for_each` set, upgrade a
module that ships its own migration, chain moves across versions, and hand a
resource over to another state. Every step ends on the same target: a plan with
**zero resource changes**.

## Layout

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `live/` | The working root - the only directory with a real state. Starts at step 1. |
| `step-1` .. `step-6`, `step-5b` | Complete snapshots, one per gesture (all CI-validated). |
| `modules/app-config/{v1,v2,v3}` | The platform team's module, three published versions. v2/v3 ship `moved.tf` + `MIGRATION.md`. |
| `adjacent/` | The billing team's root - a separate state, target of the step-6 handover. |
| `scripts/switch.sh` | Overlays a snapshot into `live/` - the state stays put. |

## Run

```sh
mise install
cd live
terraform init
terraform apply            # step 1 - the starting point (4 SSM parameters)
cd ..
scripts/switch.sh step-2   # then: cd live && terraform init && terraform plan
```

## Steps

| Step | Gesture | Mechanism | What the plan proves |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Starting point: flat root, drifted naming, a foreign resource | - | 4 parameters created |
| 2 | Rename to the naming convention | `moved` (root) | `has moved to`, 0 change |
| 3 | Migrate the config parameter to the platform module | `moved` (consumer-written) | move into `module.app_config`, 0 change |
| 4 | Absorb the `for_each` flag set | one `moved` on the resource address | every instance moves, 0 change |
| 5 | Module upgrade v1 -> v2 (internal rename) | `moved.tf` shipped BY the module | move replayed without touching this root |
| 5b | Jump to v3 - even straight from v1 | chained `moved` blocks | the full lineage replays in one plan |
| 6 | Hand the billing parameter to its owner | `removed` + `destroy = false`, then `import` in `adjacent/` | forgotten here, adopted there, never destroyed |

Between steps, `terraform state pull | jq '.resources[].name'` shows what the
refactor did to the state - and `git log` is the only history of the moves:
an applied `moved` block leaves no marker in the state.

## Producer / consumer rules demonstrated

- A **published module** ships its migrations (`moved.tf` + `MIGRATION.md`) and
  **keeps them for the lifetime of the major**: the chain is the upgrade path,
  removing a hop is a breaking change.
- A **root module** writes `moved` blocks for its own refactors and cleans them
  up once applied in every environment.
- `moved` cannot cross state files and requires the same resource type on both
  sides. The cross-state workflow is `removed` (without destroy) + `import`.

## Troubleshooting

- `terraform init` is required after every switch that changes a module source.
- The `adjacent/` import block hardcodes the default `name_prefix`; align it if
  you changed the variable.

## Going further

- [`terraform-query-import`](../terraform-query-import/) - the declarative
  `import` and `query` side of adopting existing infrastructure.
- [`terraform-secrets-out-of-state`](../terraform-secrets-out-of-state/) - what
  the state persists, and how to keep secrets out of it.

## References

- [Refactoring (moved blocks)](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/modules/develop/refactoring) - rename/split/chain rules, instance keys, and why removing a `moved` block is a breaking change.
- [Remove a resource from state (removed block)](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/state/remove) - `destroy = false` semantics and why the block beats `state rm`.
- [Refactor across state files](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/state/refactor) - the `removed` + `import` handover and the `state mv -state-out` legacy path.
- [Import block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) - declarative adoption, previewable at plan.
- [aws_ssm_parameter](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs/resources/ssm_parameter) - the resource used everywhere here; its import id is the parameter name.

#### Structure (conducteur timé en cours de production, jalons Phase 2)

Fil prio (~35 min de cœur) :

| Bloc | Support | Objectif |
|---|---|---|
| OPEN | cam | accueil, format, invite chat, partage d'écran confirmé |
| WHY (S0) | slide | la peur du state ; micro-historique : state mv impératif → moved v1.1 |
| WHAT (S1) | slide | state = table d'association ; moved = édition déclarative de la table |
| HOW-1 · rename | terminal | démo 1 : mise en conformité de nommage, state pull avant/après, plan « no changes » |
| HOW-1bis · sous le capot | terminal | deep-dive : manipulation des références, delta vs terraform state mv, propagation multi-env |
| HOW-2 · split | terminal | démo 2 : migration vers le module de l'équipe plateforme pour rentrer en conformité |
| LIMITES (S2) | slide | même type requis · pas cross-state (relais = removed + import, cf. live S25) · rétention child/root · force-replacement |
| CLOSE | slide récap + CTA | matrice de choix par cas d'usage (moved / state mv / removed+import), repo |

Bonus numérotés (joués si avance au jalon mi-live, dans l'ordre) :
1. `for_each` impacté par le split.
2. Bump v2 du sous-module : `moved.tf` + `migration.md` livrés par le module ; v3 enchaînée = cascade de moved (saut de majors).
3. `removed` (`destroy = false`) sur la ressource intruse + ré-adoption par bloc `import`.
4. Dogfooding : refactorer un exemple existant du repo, puis `git restore` (décision au pré-vol).

Beats verrouillés, coupes et phrases de sortie : figés en Phase 2 avec les mesures du lab.
input.new_string:
#### Conducteur timé (fil prio 35 min, créneau ≤ 1h, T0 = 13h00)

Jalons = heure de **sortie** de bloc. Les bonus remplacent les coupes : on ajoute si avance au jalon T0+22, on ne coupe plus en retard.

| Sortie | Bloc | Support | Objectif |
|---|---|---|---|
| T0+2 | OPEN | cam | accueil, format, invite chat ; **partage d'écran confirmé au retour programme** |
| T0+8 | WHY (S0) | slide | la peur du refactoring : le state suit le code à la trace ; historique en 1 slide (`state mv` impératif → `moved` v1.1) |
| T0+11 | WHAT (S1) | slide | state = table d'association blocs ⇔ ressources ; `moved` = édition déclarative, versionnée, relue de la table |
| T0+16 | HOW-1 · rename | terminal | step-2 : mise en conformité de nommage ; `switch.sh` (bascule scriptée), plan lu à l'écran, apply |
| T0+22 | HOW-1bis · sous le capot | terminal | `state pull` avant/après : **aucune trace du moved appliqué, le suivi = git** ; delta vs `state mv` (impératif, un env à la fois, non relu) ; démo d'échec : moved cross-type, erreur lue |
| T0+30 | HOW-2 · split | terminal | step-3 : migration vers le module de l'équipe plateforme (conformité) ; moved écrit par le consommateur, init + plan « no changes » ; règle de nettoyage root |
| T0+35 | LIMITES (S2) | slide | même type par défaut (`ResourceWithMoveState` = l'exception) · pas cross-state → relais `removed`+`import` (live S25) · rétention child garde tout / root nettoie · force-replacement |
| T0+37 | CLOSE | slide récap + CTA | matrice de choix (`moved` / `state mv` / `removed`+`import`) ; repo affiché |

##### Sorties de bloc
- WHY : « Le plan qui fait peur dit destroy puis create. On va lui faire dire no changes. »
- WHAT : « Le state est une table. On va arrêter de l'éditer à la main. »
- HOW-1 : « Le bloc a bougé, la ressource n'a pas bougé. »
- HOW-1bis : « Le state ne se souvient de rien. Git se souvient de tout. »
- HOW-2 : « La migration est un commit. La promotion la propage. »
- LIMITES : « moved déplace dans un state, jamais entre deux. »

##### Bonus numérotés (décision au jalon T0+22, dans l'ordre)
1. `for_each` (step-4, ~4 min) : un seul bloc moved déplace toutes les instances, une ligne par clé au plan.
2. Bump v2 puis saut v3 (step-5/5b, ~6 min) : le module livre `moved.tf` + `MIGRATION.md` ; la cascade se résout en une ligne (`a has moved to c`).
3. `removed` + `import` (step-6 + `adjacent/`, ~6 min) : l'intruse sort sans destroy, l'autre state l'adopte.
4. Dogfooding (~5 min) : refactorer un exemple existant du repo, puis `git restore` (décision au pré-vol).

##### Beats verrouillés
1. Le plan « no changes » du split, lu à l'écran (`Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy`).
2. Les deux `state pull` de HOW-1bis : la trace n'existe pas, git est le seul historique.
3. L'erreur cross-type lue à voix haute (« does not include move resource state support »).
4. Si bonus 2 joué : la ligne unique de la cascade, l'argument qui clôt le débat du nettoyage.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/bgauduch/Obsidian Vault/.claude/skills/add-editorial-slides

# Add Editorial Slides

Generate a branded HTML slide deck (interactive, browser-first) for a piece. Distinct artifact class from PNG visuals (§5.0): multi-slide, responsive 16:9, delivered as-is (opened in the browser). The skeleton fixes the frame + slide-type components; Claude assembles **semantic slides**, never absolute coordinates. A **legibility gate by per-slide inspection** + brand-review lock the result. Content FR.

## SSoT - read at runtime, never restate

| Concern | Source |
|---|---|
| Slides format spec (composition rules, slide-types catalogue, layout, navigation) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/03-Design-system.md` §5.7 |
| Format registry (dims, naming, home) | `03-Design-system.md` §5.0 |
| Color tokens + WCAG ratios | `03-Design-system.md` §1.1 / §1.2 |
| Executable skeleton (frame + slide-type classes + slot markers + nav) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/skeletons/slides.html` |
| HTML->PNG renderer (QA, supports `?slide=N`) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/_pipeline/render-html.mjs` |
| Voice (positive phrasing §2.7, Golden Circle arc §2.9) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md` |
| Asset naming, piece link, lint gate | `02-Areas/Éditorial/CLAUDE.md` |

Reverse-engineering from an existing deck is forbidden (BGA CLAUDE.md Asset production contract). The skeleton is the only structural base.

## Input

`--piece <path>` (required). Source = the piece body: `## Accroche` (hook), `## Corps` (Why → How → What), key bullets, tables.
`--scope intro|full` (optional, default `intro`): `intro` = short deck (~5 slides: title, context/Why, key cases or points, one synthesis table, transition); `full` = cover the conductor.
`--out <path>` (optional): override output; default `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/slides-<subject>.html`.

## Workflow

### 1. Read the piece + outline the deck
- Read the piece. Extract: the hook (`## Accroche`), the Why → How → What spine, key bullets, any tables (reuse **verbatim** as `table` slides).
- Build a slide list: pick a slide-type per idea via the **§5.7 archetype heuristic** (content→format table, read at runtime). Catalogue, archetypes and heuristic live in §5.7 only - never restate the mapping here. `intro` scope: keep ~5 slides. Positive phrasing (§2.7), one idea per line, Golden Circle arc (§2.9).
- Lead slide = `title` (piece H1 + a key fragment in `<span class="hl">` + a framing `sub`). Close = `flow` or a `title` transition ("place à la suite").

### 2. Clone the skeleton
- Copy `Brand/skeletons/slides.html` → `<out>` (default `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/slides-<subject>.html`, `<subject>` kebab-case from the piece). Collision → suffix `-2` and warn.

### 3. Fill the slides region (semantic HTML, never coordinates)
- Replace content between `<!-- slot:slides:start -->` / `<!-- slot:slides:end -->` (markers only, never line numbers). Missing/orphan marker → explicit abort, no fallback.
- One `<section class="slide">` per slide, first one `active`. Use the skeleton's component classes per slide-type (§5.7). **Add `.slide-logo` (wordmark top-right) on every slide except `title`** (the cover carries the big wordmark) - the skeleton reference slides show the markup. Reuse the piece's tables as-is for `table` slides; emphasise the key cell with `class="em"` and the last row is auto-highlighted.
- Compose HTML that lays itself out (no fixed heights/positions; text must wrap). Keep each slide concise to fit the frame - the engine does not shrink the font; split a dense slide in two rather than overflow.

### 4. Legibility gate (per slide, blocking)
- For each slide N: `node "02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/_pipeline/render-html.mjs" "<out>?slide=N" /tmp/<subject>-<N>.png 1280 720`, then **Read the PNG**. Check: no overlap, no text outside its frame or truncated, legible hierarchy (kicker < h1/h2), the slide fits. Any anomaly → fix the HTML (concision, split), re-render. The PNG is authoritative, not the HTML.

### 5. Brand-review gate
- Run the `brand-review` skill: `--visual <out> --visual-png <representative slide PNG> --text <piece>`.
- Pre-check (blocking, ADR-001 - the procedure lives in `check-colors.mjs`, never restated here): run it on **every slide**, `node "02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/_pipeline/check-colors.mjs" <out>?slide=N` for N in 1..total. A slide-1 sample is NOT a gate: a defect that lives in one slide-type ships undetected. Measured on the skeleton itself (2026-08-10): `?slide=1` green while 2 of 18 slides failed V4.
- Verdict ≠ PRÊT (incl. V9 legibility) → fix, re-render, re-review. Steps 4+5: max 3 loops, then surface the residual.

### 6. Wire the piece (idempotent)
- In `## Notes production`, add/refresh one line pointing to the deck: ``Deck de slides : `assets/slides-<subject>.html` (ouvrir au navigateur ; flèches / clic, `f` plein écran, `l` mode pointeur).`` Re-run with the same deck = no-op. Slides are a live-support artifact, not a `## Visuels` PNG entry - keep them out of the `## Visuels` brief.
- Run `python3 02-Areas/Éditorial/scripts/lint-editorial.py --file <piece> --apply`; report residual violations.

### 7. Return
- Deck path. Slide count + slide-types used. Legibility gate: OK | fixed (n loops). Brand-review verdict (+ manual residuals). Piece wiring: applied | already present.

## Rules
- **Read §5.7 Règles de composition before outlining**, not just the slide-type catalogue. They decide *which* slide exists; the catalogue only decides what it is made of. They are read at runtime, never restated here - a rule written there applies to the next generation without depending on the agent's memory.
- **Two blocking slides**, checked before returning: a destination teaser and a récap + CTA. A live deck without them is non-conforming (retex S30: both planned, neither prepared, neither played).
- Skeleton = structural SSoT. No reverse-engineering of existing decks; changing the frame or slide-types = amend §5.7 + the skeleton first.
- **Layout delegated to CSS**: never absolute positioning, never hand-computed coordinates. Compose semantic slides with the skeleton classes.
- Colors = closed whitelists: hex §1.1, translucent derivatives §1.1bis. Missing value → STOP, amend the design-system. Alpha never on ink.
- Text on light background respects WCAG §1.2. The amber accent token is decorative only (bars, arrows), never text (§7).
- Interactive HTML is the deliverable; the PNG is QA-only (no delivery PNG). An illegible slide is never delivered, even if tokens/WCAG pass.
- One deck = one `slides-<subject>.html` (§5.0, home `Éditorial/assets/`, ADR-006).
- Output FR; English limited to this SKILL.md.

Wordmark compact `.slide-logo` (BGA · Consulting) en haut à droite sur **toutes les slides, `title` comprise** - identité stable de slide en slide (rév. 2026-08-13, relecture S33 : le grand wordmark central de la cover « se baladait » au passage cover → slide 2). **Kicker = langage lecteur**, jamais un code de production (S0, S1, T0+NN). 553 554 **Navigation** : flèches / clic (gauche-droite) / espace ; plein écran touche `f` ; compteur de slides. Gate QA : `?slide=N` affiche la slide N seule, chrome masqué. 555 556 **Mode pointeur** (touche `l`, sortie par `l` ou `Échap`) : le clic cesse de naviguer, le curseur devient un marqueur ambre, et maintenir le bouton trace un trait qui s'efface en ~1,2 s. Sert à désigner et souligner à la souris pendant une démo sans changer de slide par accident. L'ambre reste ici décoratif (§1.2). L'indicateur de raccourcis reflète le mode actif. 557 558 **Surligneur de titre** : fragment `.hl` en **bande pleine arrondie** (`background-color: accent-soft` + `border-radius`), rév. 2026-08-13 (relecture S33) : la bande partielle « peinte depuis le bas » (§5.8) rendait un bord haut carré/tronqué, perçu comme un bug d'affichage. L'aération inter-lignes est portée par le `line-height` des titres (h1/h2 **1.38**), qui doit couvrir la boîte de fond inline de Manrope (~1.36em) - en dessous, la bande d'une ligne mange les jambages de la ligne au-dessus. Règle bloquante de légibilité. Le carrousel et l'event-banner (§5.8, filière PDF/PNG) conservent leur technique propre. 559 560 **Tokens / police** : Manrope (titres, labels), JetBrains Mono (kicker, identifiants techniques). Ambre `#C68A14` décoratif uniquement (filets, barres, flèches), jamais en texte. Texte sur aplats `bg` / `surface` only, WCAG §1.2 sur le composite (§1.1bis). Tokens §1.1 et dérivés §1.1bis = whitelists fermées. 561 562 **Assets** : nommage, home et squelette → §5.0 (type éditorial par-pièce, ADR-006). Génération : skill `add-editorial-slides`. 563 564 ### 5.8 Carrousel LinkedIn (document post) 565 566 Carrousel de repurpose (retex de live, décomposition d'un sujet en pages), publié comme document LinkedIn. Format, dims, nommage, home, squelette : §5.0. Même filière HTML auto-layout CSS (jamais de coordonnée à la main) ; assemblage du contenu via le skill `add-editorial-carousel` (ou hand-craft depuis le squelette). 567 568 **Nature** : un fichier HTML, N pages portrait **4:5 (1080x1350)** empilées (emprise feed mobile maximale). Livraison = **PDF** `carousel-.pdf` (1 page HTML = 1 page PDF, via print CSS `@page` + `break-after`). Le PNG par page est transient : gate de légibilité (`?page=N`) + input éventuel d'un PDF assemblé d'images. Texte gros, lisible en thumbnail. 569 570 **Colonne vertébrale narrative (principe 2.9, Why → How → What)** : page 1 = hook (*Why*), pages de corps = mécanisme (*How*), avant-dernière = principe à retenir (*What*), dernière = CTA. Le carrousel raconte une histoire, pas une suite d'écrans. 571 572 **Règles de composition** (distillées des relectures de carrousel, arbitrages Baptiste 2026-08-10 et 2026-08-17). Elles s'appliquent avant le catalogue : elles décident *quelle* page on compose, le catalogue décide *avec quoi*. 573 - **Autoporteur** : chaque page se comprend sans les précédentes et sans avoir vu le live. Une série, un acronyme ou un live antérieur se définit dans la page, ou gagne une page dédiée (liste des volets : nom, version, date, renvoi vers les replays). 574 - **Une page = une idée = un *why*** : une page répond à une seule question. Deux idées → deux pages, ou une coupe. Séquence d'ensemble : constat → réponses → à retenir → CTA. 575 - **Titre = le *why*, factuel** : le titre nomme ce que la page apporte. Figure de style, personnification, jeu de mots : interdits, ils masquent le message (rejets S33 : « le plan se tait, le state parle »). 576 - **Kicker = nature de la page** (le constat, le mécanisme, démo N, les cas d'usage, à retenir, la série). Jamais le making-of ni le ressenti d'auteur. Les démos se numérotent. 577 - **Une page de démo dit ce que le mécanisme apporte**, jamais seulement ce qui a été tapé. La sortie de commande est la preuve ; le titre et la carte d'état portent la leçon (S32 : « détecter ce qui vit hors du state », et non « casser le site »). 578 - **Exemple de code = le cas d'usage cible**, copiable tel quel, repris du lab `final/`. Jamais les étapes intermédiaires de la démo ni les artefacts de mise en scène. 579 - **Zéro répétition** : une idée figure sur une seule page. Passe anti-répétition avant livraison ; toute reformulation d'un beat déjà posé se supprime. Redite = demande explicite de l'auteur.

# Session Handoff

Make the session resumable from a cold context: the rich trace lands in the project's **tracking file** (it owns priorities), nothing is lost, the next session starts from one short prompt.

Honors: `feedback_tracking_files_always_uptodate`, `feedback_para_archivage_extract_forward_looking`, `feedback_scope_discipline_endorsed_actions`, `feedback_ssot_no_restate_in_skills`, `feedback_git_mv_then_edit_restage`. Lesson routing per global `CLAUDE.md` (memory vs `tasks/lessons.md`).

## 1. Scan the session
`git status --short` + `git log --oneline` (this session's commits) + `git diff --stat`. List built / changed / decided / discovered. Separate MY changes from unrelated working-tree edits (parallel sessions) - never sweep those in.

## 2. Locate the tracking file (SSoT for priorities)
Project living doc: backlog / `tasks/todo.md` / project-main / MoC / PLAN. Glob the working dir + common names. Ambiguous or none → ask which (or to create one). Match its language for everything below. An Area doctrine is a durable living doc, not a session tracker: it may receive the §4 reconcile (backlog items with triggers, dated journal) but NEVER the §7 resume region.

## 3. Verify state (oracle)
Find + run the project's check command (tests / validator / linter / build / typecheck). Record the exact command + result. Red → fix in scope or flag it prominently in the prompt (don't hand off a broken tree silently).

## 4. Reconcile the tracking file (the dump)
Edit it to carry:
- One-line **status/progress** (themes done/total, % if used).
- **Done** items → mark resolved + trace (commit / ADR / file).
- **Decisions** taken + alternatives discarded + revisit-trigger.
- **Every leftover / deferred / debt** → a **live, trackable item** under the right priority, each annotated with **value** and **trigger** ("do only if X", "revisit when Y / at volume ×5"). Track **debt** as its own category. Never leave future work living only in a journal entry, a resolved item's prose, or a to-be-deleted note.
- A dated **journal entry**: done / decisions / deviations from plan / frictions / reste. Past-tense only - no "à venir"/"next" inside a journal line (forward-looking → live item; a stale "upcoming" line contradicts newer entries).

## 5. Route lessons
Corrections + frictions this session → formulate a rule that prevents recurrence. Cross-project → auto-memory (`feedback_*`); repo-specific → `tasks/lessons.md`. Iterate an existing rule, don't stack a duplicate.

## 6. Traceability gate (before any deletion)
Enumerate each decision / discovery / leftover / blocker and map each to a durable home (tracking item / ADR / subtree CLAUDE.md / schema / code docstring / commit / memory). Anything living **only in chat or a disposable note** → persist first. Only then may a disposable scratch/plan note be `git rm`'d - surface + confirm. Re-stage after any `git mv`+Edit.

## 7. Persist + emit the resume prompt → tracking file (disposable) + `pbcopy` + print
Write the lean prompt into the tracking file in a **disposable anchored region**, just under the H1/frontmatter so a cold start sees it first - **only where the note's own structure declares that section**. Vault: templates are a closed whitelist (`99-Templates/`, resolved by `type:`), and only `type: project` `role: main` declares it. Template silent, or note type absent from the map → **no write at all**: `pbcopy` + print + an explicit warning ("prompt en presse-papier uniquement, pas de section Reprise dans le template de cette note"). NEVER create the section where the template lacks it, and never in an Area doctrine or a Resource. Read the region before writing: orphan or duplicated anchors → abort, no fallback write (vault: hybrid-editing contract). Heading in the tracking file's language (vault note → FR), e.g.:
```
## 🔄 Reprise (jetable - régénéré à chaque handoff, pas d'historique)
<!-- skill:handoff:resume:start -->
_MAJ <YYYY-MM-DD>_

…prompt…
<!-- skill:handoff:resume:end -->
```
**Overwrite** the region every run (replace, never append - only the latest matters). Re-read after writing: stamp = today, exactly one anchor pair. A stamp older than today means the overwrite missed - fail loudly, do not proceed to §8. Also `pbcopy` + print (clipboard is volatile; the note is the persistence). Content, short + paste-ready:
- 1-line project + state ("X done, committed").
- **Reload list (cold-start warm-up)** = the explicit set of links to open before acting, drawn from what actually proved useful this session: files touched (§1), SSoT/pattern docs consulted, reference notes / sub-projects, relevant memories by name. **Tracking file first** (SSoT for priorities + journal). Render each as a real link - wikilink `[[Note]]` / `[[Note#Section]]` for a note, backtick path for a non-note file (per `feedback_obsidian_reference_links`) - plus a 3-5 word *why*. This is the materialized context-rewarm: keep it to the 5-8 that matter, not an index of the repo.
- **Oracle command** (run to confirm green) + last known result.
- **Blockers / prerequisites** (env, MCP, auth, login) - or "none".
- **Next step** = the single top unresolved item: one line + pointer to its tracking item (e.g. "détail : P1"). Never restate the item's content (attachments, sub-steps) - it drifts between handoffs; the item is the only home. No meta-commentary about the rule in the note itself.
- Key conventions/gotchas + "start in plan mode, confirm scope before acting".

## 8. Checkpoint commit (restore point BEFORE trim)
Commit the non-destructive work so far - reconcile (§4) + resume region (§7) + in-scope files - per project convention (this vault: on `main`, dedicated commit, no branch). This is the **restore point** before the lossy compaction: if §9 misfires, `git checkout <this commit> -- <tracking file>`.

## 9. Compaction pass (synthetic, no loss, no dup) - gated by §6
Tracking notes bloat (modif history, verbose steps) and that hurts cold-start context elsewhere. Trim, but **only what already has a durable home** (§6) - never lose forward-looking content. **Surface the diff before applying.**
- **Resolved items** → one line + pointer (`✅ RÉSOLU <date> (commit/ADR) - <what>`); drop verbose `(description initiale…)` blocks.
- **De-dup** item-prose vs journal → one home (the item line carries the pointer, the journal carries the dated narrative; not both in full).
- **Journal** entries older than active relevance → condense or move to a `… Journal archive` note.
- **Target shape**: where the project fixes its own note structure (vault: `99-Templates/`), that structure wins - place each element in the whitelisted section that fits, add none. Elsewhere, top→bottom: frontmatter · 🔄 Reprise/Resume (jetable) · Statut/Status (1 line) · active priorities P0..P3 (value+trigger) · decisions (+ ADR refs) · resolved (one-liners + pointer) · journal (recent, terse) · debt.
Commit the compaction separately (distinct from §8).

## 10. Working-tree hygiene
Report uncommitted changes. Commit only in-scope files (project convention: per-group / per-task). Leave parallel-session files untouched.

## Rules
Terse. Reference SSoT/pointers, never restate values. **Persist (commit) before you trim.** Confirm before deleting or trimming anything. Surface every inference before writing.

Restauration faite, audit terminé. **Et j'ai trouvé le point décisif : Renovate.**

## Task 1 - le plan versions

**Les données** (pin `mise.toml` vs `required_version`) :

| Exemple | pin | plancher | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| check-health · check-conditional-policy | 1.5.0 | >= 1.5.0 | pile le plancher |
| secrets-out-of-state | 1.11.4 | >= 1.11.1 | +patch, **justifié en commentaire** (bug #36619) |
| aws-multi-env · actions · actions-lambda · query-import | 1.14.8/9 | >= 1.14 | pile le plancher |
| deferred-actions/02-after | 1.16.0-alpha | >= 1.16.0 | pile, gelé par Renovate |
| **aws-budget-cutoff** | **1.15.6** | **~> 1.9** | **6 minors au-dessus** |
| **module-testing** | **1.15.6** | **>= 1.9.0** | **6 minors au-dessus** |
| state-refactoring | (supprimé par moi) | >= 1.7.0 | à poser |

**Le point décisif** : `.github/renovate.json` bumpe **tous** les pins stables chaque semaine. Seuls les `-alpha|beta|rc` sont gelés. Les 2 « dérives » ne sont pas des erreurs d'auteur : Renovate les a fait monter. Donc la règle « pin = plancher » **se fait défaire toutes les semaines**, sauf à geler mise sous `examples/` — et alors plus rien ne teste tes exemples contre un Terraform récent.

**Ce que ça révèle : les deux valeurs répondent à deux questions différentes.**
- `required_version` = **le contrat**. « la version minimum où ce code marche ». Sémantique, ne dérive jamais, c'est *elle* qui illustre la feature.
- pin `mise.toml` = **la version testée**. Ce que toi et la CI avez réellement joué. Elle doit avancer, sinon une régression Terraform 1.16 passe inaperçue.

Sous cet angle, épingler mise au plancher est un piège : tu ne testerais plus jamais que la plus vieille version supportée.

**Ma reco - option A, mais avec la règle écrite** :
1. Racine garde `terraform` (version testée courante, bumpée par Renovate) + `tflint` + `trivy`.
2. Un exemple n'override **que s'il en a besoin**, et le commentaire dit pourquoi : alpha assumée (`deferred-actions`), version bloquée sur un bug connu (`secrets`), démonstration d'un comportement ancien.
3. Le **plancher vit en `required_version`**, jamais dans mise. C'est ce que lit un praticien.
4. Nettoyage : les overrides qui ne diffèrent plus de la racine sautent (budget-cutoff, module-testing, actions×2, query, multi-env, check×2 — à valider un par un).
5. Règle codifiée dans `AGENTS.md` §Toolchain, sinon elle redérive.

**Interaction à trancher avec toi** : `AGENTS.md` dit « tasks replace Makefiles » (`mise run <task>`). Si je te propose une tâche de démo (voir Task 2), elle a besoin d'un `mise.toml` dans l'exemple — même sans override de version. Ça peut militer pour ta piste B (un fichier partout). À arbitrer ensemble.

## Task 2 - switch.sh, et le coup de tournevis

**Ce qu'il fait aujourd'hui**, `./scripts/switch.sh step-2` :
1. copie les `.tf` actuels de `live/` dans un temp
2. affiche le **diff** temp → snapshot `step-2/`
3. remplace les `.tf` de `live/` par ceux de `step-2/`
4. **ne touche jamais** `live/terraform.tfstate` — c'est tout le principe : le state reste, le code change

**La friction que tu sens** : le script se lance depuis la racine de l'exemple, `terraform` depuis `live/`. Donc à l'antenne tu fais `cd ..` / `cd live` en boucle. C'est exactement le type d'hésitation qui t'a coûté 5 moments au S33.

**Trois options, ma reco en 3** :

| | Mécanique | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Deux terminaux : switch à gauche, terraform à droite | le diff et le plan sont sur deux écrans, l'audience perd le lien de cause à effet |
| 2 | Un terminal, `cd` à la main | ce que tu vis, ça hésite |
| 3 | **Une tâche `mise run step 2`** depuis n'importe où : affiche le diff → `init` si la source de module a changé → `plan`. Les commandes s'échoent avant de s'exécuter | un geste par palier, zéro `cd`, la chaîne diff → plan → « no changes » se lit d'un bloc |

En 3, tu gardes la main : le `apply` reste séparé, tu le tapes quand tu veux. Le script ne fait que ce qui est mécanique et répétitif.

Je code l'option 3 ? Et tu tranches A ou B sur les versions — j'applique dans la foulée.

Sinon, on ne s'emmerde pas, étant donné qu'on a les pins spécifiques dans le code du provider, c'est suffisant pour indiquer la version au minimum. Dans ce cas, on peut se dire qu'on a juste une version Terraform qui couvre tous les cas d'usage à la racine. Qu'en penses-tu par rapport à l'état actuel des choses ? Tous les exemples sont autoporteurs et autonomes, donc à la racine, on s'en fout. Donc je ne suis pas certain de comprendre ta remarque.

**1. Versions : oui, c'est exactement ma reco.** Ta formulation la dit mieux que moi : le plancher est déjà dans le code (`required_version`), donc mise n'a pas à le redire. Une version Terraform à la racine qui couvre tous les cas, override seulement quand l'exemple ne *peut pas* tourner dessus (alpha assumée, bug connu). **2. Mon « interaction à trancher » était confuse, elle n'existe pas.** Je pensais à une tâche `mise run` qui aurait forcé un `mise.toml` dans l'exemple. Mais en vérifiant : `switch.sh` résout sa racine depuis son propre chemin, donc **`../scripts/switch.sh step-2` marche depuis `live/`**. Tu ne quittes jamais `live/`, pas de `cd`, pas de tâche, pas de fichier. La remarque tombe.

**3. Ton objection sur le state est juste, et mon option 3 réglait le mauvais problème.**

Le vrai défaut n'est pas le nombre de terminaux. C'est que **code et state sont deux axes indépendants** :

- `switch.sh` déplace l'axe **code**
- `terraform apply` déplace l'axe **state**

Rien ne garantit qu'ils restent alignés. Si un palier casse à l'antenne, tu ne peux pas revenir : le code se rembobine, le state non. Et pour répéter ce soir, tu dois `destroy` + tout réappliquer à chaque tour.

**Ce que la structure du lab offre gratuitement, et que je n'ai pas exploité** : après le step-1, **aucun palier ne touche AWS**. Ce sont tous des mouvements de state (c'est la thèse du live : « un plan no changes »). Backend local ⇒ le state est un simple fichier.

Donc **rembobiner la démo = recopier un fichier. Zéro appel AWS, instantané.** Je vérifie que ça tient techniquement avant de te le proposer :

**Mesuré** : serial 1 → 2 → retour à 1 par `cp`, et `plan` répond `No changes`. Terraform accepte le state rembobiné sans broncher (backend local, pas de lock distant).

**Le coup de tournevis, version corrigée** - trois verbes, un seul terminal, tu restes dans `live/` :

| Commande | Quand | Ce que ça fait |
|---|---|---|
| `../scripts/switch.sh save` | une fois, après l'apply du step-1 | snapshot du state dans `.baseline/` (gitignoré) |
| `../scripts/switch.sh step-N` | à chaque palier | diff des `.tf` + bascule, puis **affiche la commande exacte à taper** (`terraform plan`, ou `init && plan` s'il détecte un changement de source de module) |
| `../scripts/switch.sh reset` | répétition, ou incident à l'antenne | code → step-1, state → baseline, state d'`adjacent` supprimé. **Instantané, zéro appel AWS** |

Ce que ça débloque :
- **répéter ce soir** : la chaîne complète en boucle, chaque tour coûte une copie de fichier au lieu d'un `destroy` + réapply
- **filet à l'antenne** : un palier plante, `reset`, tu reprends — pas de trou de 4 minutes en direct
- **le geste reste le tien** : le script ne joue jamais `plan` ni `apply`, il prépare et il dit quoi taper

Cohérent parce que **après le step-1, aucun palier ne touche AWS** : tout est mouvement de state. C'est la thèse du live qui rend le rembobinage gratuit.

Go pour : (a) le nettoyage versions comme convenu + règle dans `AGENTS.md`, (b) `switch.sh` v2 avec `save`/`reset` ?

Ok pour le nettoyage des versions convenues. Tu as raison, je retire. J'ai inventé un problème.

**Ce que je faisais** : `save`/`reset` servaient à rembobiner sans `destroy`. Mais rembobiner coûte ~20 s sur 4 paramètres SSM (`destroy` + `switch step-1` + `apply`). Je t'ai vendu une machinerie pour économiser 20 secondes.

**Et c'est pire que superflu** : un helper qui restaure un fichier de state à la main **contredit la thèse du live**. Tu passes une heure à dire « on arrête d'éditer le state à la main, on le fait en déclaratif », et l'outil de la démo ferait exactement l'inverse. À l'écran ça saborde le message.

`switch.sh` reste comme il est : bascule + diff. Une seule chose méritait un fix, sans verbe ni fichier en plus : après un switch qui change une source de module (steps 3, 5, 5b), `plan` échoue si tu n'as pas fait `init`. input.command:

import io
p="AGENTS.md"; s=io.open(p,encoding="utf-8").read()
old="""- **Root `mise.toml`** pins repo-wide tools (`tflint`, `trivy`) plus a default `terraform`. **Per-example `mise.toml`** overrides only `terraform` (versions legitimately differ per example) and inherits the rest, since mise merges every `mise.toml` from the cwd up to the repo root."""
new="""- **Root `mise.toml`** pins the toolchain for the whole repo: `tflint`, `trivy`, and the single `terraform` version every example is tested against. mise merges every `mise.toml` from the cwd up to the repo root, so an example inherits it by default.
- **The floor and the tested version are two different things - do not conflate them.** An example's minimum Terraform version is declared where a reader looks for it: `required_version` in its `.tf`, with a comment naming the feature that sets the floor. The `mise.toml` pin is the version CI and the author actually ran, and it moves forward (Renovate) so a regression in a newer Terraform is caught.
- **A per-example `mise.toml` overrides `terraform` only when the example cannot run on the root version** - e.g. an `experiment` that needs an alpha/rc. Pinning a floor there is a bug: it freezes the example on the oldest supported version and it is never tested against anything else. An example whose `mise.toml` holds only a redundant pin has no reason to exist; keep the file when it carries `[tasks]`."""
assert old in s
io.open(p,"w",encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(old,new))
print("AGENTS.md §Toolchain mis à jour")
PY

## What

New `lab` example: declarative state refactoring, one gesture per step, every step ending on a zero-change plan. Plus two repo-wide follow-ups it surfaced.

### The lab

- `live/` working root + `step-1`..`step-6` (+ `step-5b`) complete CI-validated snapshots, overlaid via `scripts/switch.sh` (no live commenting). The script prints the `.tf` diff on each switch and leaves state, lock and `.terraform/` untouched.

- `adjacent/`: separate state adopting a resource released by `removed` + `destroy = false` via an `import` block.
- Catalogue row added.

### Toolchain convention (repo-wide)

`required_version` and the mise pin answered the same question in two places, and Renovate kept walking the pins away from the floors they claimed to document. Split them:

- `required_version` carries the **contract** (minimum version illustrating the feature), commented in the `.tf`.
- Root `mise.toml` carries the **version everything is tested against** (now 1.15.6), Renovate-maintained.
- An example overrides `terraform` only when it **cannot** run on the root version - only `deferred-actions/02-after` (alpha) qualifies. Eight redundant pins removed, five `mise.toml` deleted outright, three kept for their `[tasks]`.
- Rule written into `AGENTS.md` §Toolchain; 13 docs realigned in the same commit.

## Checks

- `terraform fmt` / `validate`: 13 root modules green on 1.15.6.
- `tflint`: green.
- Core semantics measured on Terraform 1.14.8 then replayed end to end on the AWS sandbox: plan wording, no state marker after an applied move, `for_each` set move, chained moves resolved in one line, cross-type refusal, `removed` keeping the resource, `import` adopting it in the other state.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

# Terraform state refactoring - `moved`, `removed`, `import`

`lab` · tags: `terraform` `state` `moved` `removed` `import` `refactoring` `modules` `v1.7`

Refactor a live root module **without destroying anything**: rename a resource,
split the root into a platform-team module, absorb a `for_each` set, upgrade a
module that ships its own migration, chain moves across versions, and hand a
resource over to another team. Every step ends on the same target: a plan with
**zero resource changes**.

## How the lab is driven

One directory does the work, `live/`. It is the only one that ever holds a state
file, and it is the only one you `cd` into. Each step is a **complete snapshot**
of what `live/` should contain at that point, and one script swaps them in:

```sh
cd live
../scripts/switch.sh step-2     # prints the .tf diff, then replaces live/*.tf
```

The script touches **`.tf` files only**. `terraform.tfstate`,
`.terraform.lock.hcl` and `.terraform/` stay exactly where they are - that is the
whole trick: the state stays put while the code moves under it, which is what a
refactor really is. The printed diff is the lesson of the step; read it before
planning.

You never leave `live/`, and you keep typing plain Terraform commands. The script
does not run Terraform for you.

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `live/` | The working root - the only directory with a state. Starts at step 1. |
| `step-1` .. `step-6`, `step-5b` | Complete snapshots, one per gesture (all CI-validated). |
| `modules/app-config/{v1,v2,v3}` | The platform team's module, three published versions. v2/v3 ship `moved.tf` + `MIGRATION.md`. |
| `billing-team/` | Another team's root module, with **its own state file** - the other side of the step-6 handover. |
| `scripts/switch.sh` | Swaps a snapshot into `live/` and prints the diff. |

## Run it

```sh
mise install
cd live
terraform init
terraform apply                 # step 1 - the starting point, 4 SSM parameters
```

Then, for each step: swap, read the diff, plan, apply.

```sh
../scripts/switch.sh step-2
terraform plan                  # read the "has moved to" lines
terraform apply
```

`terraform init` is needed again whenever the **module source changes** - steps
3, 5 and 5b. Running it when it was not needed costs a second and changes
nothing, so when in doubt, run it.

## Steps

| Step | Gesture | Mechanism | What the plan shows | `init` first? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Starting point: flat root, drifted naming, a foreign resource | - | 4 parameters created | yes (first run) |
| 2 | Rename to the naming convention | `moved` (root) | `has moved to`, 0 change | no |
| 3 | Migrate the config parameter to the platform module | `moved` (consumer-written) | move into `module.app_config`, 0 change | **yes** |
| 4 | Absorb the `for_each` flag set | one `moved` on the resource address | one move **per instance**, 0 change | no |
| 5 | Module upgrade v1 -> v2 (internal rename) | `moved.tf` shipped BY the module | move replayed without touching this root | **yes** |
| 5b | Jump to v3 - even straight from v1 | chained `moved` blocks | the full lineage replays in one plan | **yes** |
| 6 | Hand the billing parameter to its owner | `removed` + `destroy = false`, then `import` in `billing-team/` | forgotten here, adopted there, never destroyed | no |

Step 5 and 5b are alternatives: 5 walks v1 -> v2 -> v3, 5b jumps v1 -> v3 in one
plan. Play whichever tells the story you want.

Between steps, `terraform state pull | jq '.resources[].name'` shows what the
refactor did to the state - and `git log` is the only history of the moves: an
applied `moved` block leaves **no trace** in the state.

## Step 6 in full - crossing a state boundary

`moved` edits one state; it cannot bridge two. Handing a resource to another team
is therefore a **pair** of blocks, one on each side:

```sh
# in live/ - step-6 declares `removed` with destroy = false
terraform apply      # the parameter leaves this state, AWS keeps it

cd ../billing-team   # a separate root, a separate state file
terraform init
terraform apply      # "Plan: 1 to import" -> "1 imported"
```

The resource is never destroyed and never recreated: only its owner changes. The
`import` block is a one-shot migration instruction - once applied, it can be
deleted.

## Rewind and teardown

After step 6, `live/` no longer manages the billing parameter, but the parameter
still exists on AWS. Replaying step 1 as-is therefore fails with
`ParameterAlreadyExists`. Two ways out.

**Rewind to replay the lab** - re-adopt it in `live/`:

```sh
cd ../billing-team && terraform state rm aws_ssm_parameter.billing_export   # if it was imported there
cd ../live && ../scripts/switch.sh step-1
terraform import aws_ssm_parameter.billing_export /tf-state-refactoring/billing/export-bucket
terraform apply
```

**Teardown** - destroy everything, in this order:

```sh
cd billing-team && terraform destroy    # only if the import was applied
cd ../live && terraform destroy
```

If neither state manages the parameter, delete it directly:
`aws ssm delete-parameter --name /tf-state-refactoring/billing/export-bucket`.

## Producer / consumer rules demonstrated

- A **published module** ships its migrations (`moved.tf` + `MIGRATION.md`) and
  **keeps them for the lifetime of the major**: the chain is the upgrade path,
  removing a hop is a breaking change.
- A **root module** writes `moved` blocks for its own refactors and cleans them
  up once applied in every environment.
- `moved` requires the same resource type on both sides, and stays inside one
  state. Crossing a state boundary is `removed` + `import`.

## Troubleshooting

- `terraform init` is required after every switch that changes a module source
  (steps 3, 5, 5b).
- `ParameterAlreadyExists` after step 6: see "Rewind and teardown" above.
- The `billing-team/` import block hardcodes the default `name_prefix`; align it
  if you changed the variable.

## Going further

- [`terraform-query-import`](../terraform-query-import/) - the declarative
  `import` and `query` side of adopting existing infrastructure.
- [`terraform-secrets-out-of-state`](../terraform-secrets-out-of-state/) - what
  the state persists, and how to keep secrets out of it.

## References

- [Refactoring (moved blocks)](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/modules/develop/refactoring) - rename/split/chain rules, instance keys, and why removing a `moved` block is a breaking change.
- [Remove a resource from state (removed block)](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/state/remove) - `destroy = false` semantics and why the block beats `state rm`.
- [Refactor across state files](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/state/refactor) - the `removed` + `import` handover and the `state mv -state-out` legacy path.
- [Import block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) - declarative adoption, previewable at plan.
- [aws_ssm_parameter](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs/resources/ssm_parameter) - the resource used everywhere here; its import id is the parameter name.

**Nommage** — `adjacent/` → **`billing-team/`**. Le répertoire dit maintenant *qui possède*, pas *où il est posé*. C'est le fond du step-6 : une frontière de state est une frontière de propriété.

- une section **« How the lab is driven »** : `cd live` une fois, `../scripts/switch.sh step-N`, le script ne touche que les `.tf`, le state et le lock restent — et il ne joue jamais Terraform à ta place
